cards.headline: Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities
cards.one_thing: Working capital measures short-term liquidity by subtracting current liabilities from current assets
cards.narration: Yesterday marked the week's first session. Today focuses on working capital using Mash Direct Ltd's FY2025 accounts. From Chapter 3 of *Financial Intelligence for Entrepreneurs*, working capital reflects a company's ability to meet short-term obligations. It comprises current assets (cash, inventory, receivables) and current liabilities (payables, short-term debt). The example company's accounts will illustrate how these components interact to show liquidity position.

ideas.text: Include cash, inventory, and accounts receivable

ideas.label: Current liabilities
ideas.text: Include accounts payable and short-term loans

ideas.label: Net working capital
ideas.text: Positive value indicates sufficient short-term funds

example.takeaway: Positive £60,000 working capital suggests ability to cover immediate obligations

cards.headline: Depreciation and capitalisation shape profit and asset values
cards.one_thing: Depreciation and amortisation reduce profit; capitalisation delays expense recognition, boosting short-term profit.
cards.narration: Yesterday’s working capital analysis with Mash Direct Ltd showed how cash flow and asset management interact. Today, focus shifts to how depreciation, amortisation, and capitalisation decisions impact financial statements. Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 accounts illustrate how allocating asset costs over time (depreciation) and treating expenses as assets (capitalisation) affect profit and balance sheet values.

ideas.label: Amortisation

ideas.label: Capitalisation
ideas.text: Recording expenses as assets, not immediate costs.

cards.headline: Build D&A and capitalisation report for Around Noon Ltd using FY2024 accounts
cards.one_thing: D&A and capitalisation reports require accurate asset valuation and depreciation methods aligned with accounting standards
cards.narration: Yesterday’s working capital analysis for Mash Direct Ltd links to today’s focus on depreciation and capitalisation. Using Chapters 6 and 7, create a report for Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 accounts. This involves identifying assets, applying depreciation rules, and determining capitalisation thresholds. The report must reflect non-current assets, accumulated depreciation, and related liabilities. Ensure consistency with the company’s financial statements and accounting policies.

ideas.label: Capitalisation Thresholds
